findings.title: Committed 2026-10-05 full-run record contradicts the canonical gate and omits the domain evidence
findings.detail: The falcon repo's durable record of the 2026-10-05 full-domain run (docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261005-0354-full-main-e267ce1) still says 'Verdict: GO WITH CONDITIONS' while carrying P0 x1/P1 x7; the pack's shared gate rule (tools/lib_findings.py:149-165) makes any P0 NO-GO, and the canonical pack run for the same audit (runs/falcon-20261005-full-main-e267ce1) says NO-GO. The committed copy also presents the full-domain findings under profile 'focused-security-supply-chain-ci' with promptCount 4 and no per-domain reports, and its follow_up_register keeps all 34 findings 'open'. Two newer canonical runs (the 20261009 full run and the 20261011 post-merge verification) have never been committed to docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/, so the newest durable record in the repository remains a P0-bearing run whose gate is wrong. Per docs/runbooks/AUDIT_RUN_LIFECYCLE.md rule 1 (never rewrite a committed run folder) the fix is an appended dated reconciliation note and/or publishing the newer runs to supersede it, plus a publish-time check that a P0-bearing run cannot emit GO/GO WITH CONDITIONS while unresolved.

findings.title: full_domain.py hardcodes profile=base and records area codes as lenses; falcon-lab coverage is not representable
findings.detail: tools/full_domain.py writes "profile": "base" unconditionally (lines 203, 219) and "lenses": [d["area"] for d in domains] (line 224), so the run manifest lists 43 area codes under 'lenses' and records no lens IDs. The pack's falcon-lab profile (profiles/falcon-lab.md, profiles/falcon-lab.manifest.json:29-31, prompts/MASTER_RUNNER_FALCON_LAB.md) documents 46 prompts (incl. 41 EVID, 42 XREPO, 43 FLEET, 44 DQ) plus five lens overlays (ND/REV/INTG/LIVE/ADV) and cannot be driven or recorded by the base full-domain driver; tools/check_run.sh:47-52 never requires the falcon-lab extras because profile != falcon-lab. Both the prior and the current 'full' falcon runs are therefore the base 42-prompt set, and coverage claims overstate what was audited. Fix: add a --profile option, emit the falcon-lab manifest shape (lens IDs/targets/status, waves) when auditing falcon, and validate the manifest against the falcon-lab example; or record an explicit, documented scope reduction.
evidence: tools/check_run.sh:47-52 — falcon-lab extras gated on profile

findings.title: Run id does not start with the timestamp required by the consumer repo's lifecycle check
findings.detail: tools/full_domain.py:185-191 prefixes the repo name in default_run() although its own comment says run ids must start YYYYMMDD-HHMM- to satisfy consumer CI. Falcon's automation/validation/audit_run_lifecycle.sh:120-122 enforces ^[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{4}- and the already-published runs required a dedicated rename commit (falcon PR #45). The current run id falcon-20261011-0416-full-f5cb7c9 fails the regex (reproduced), so publishing it unchanged into docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/ fails the repo's run check. Fix: emit <timestamp>-<mode>-<branch>-<sha7> (repo recorded in scope.name only) or auto-rename at publish; tools/publish_audit.py already defaults to a conforming timestamp-first id. Add a publish-time regex assertion.

findings.title: Domain report and findings array disagree on a finding status inside the same 20261009 run artifact
findings.detail: In runs/falcon-20261009-2117-full-08e20d1/_domains/02_architecture_runtime_topology.json the embedded report says 'ARCH-P2-001 - Declared container hardening lags the running containers (verified fixed)' with 'Status: verified-fixed', while the same file's findings array records ARCH-P2-001 as 'open'; both follow-up registers (the 20261009 run and the 20261011 verification run) carry 'open'. Live evidence at f5cb7c9 supports fixed (falcon_container_drift{kind="security"} 0 on a 04:18Z run; live no-new-privileges on all inspected central/probe containers), so an already-fixed finding remains open in the register while the report claims closure. This is the same report-vs-register contradiction class that produced ORCH-P2-001. Fix: reconcile the register with a dated note (append-only) and add a check_run.sh cross-check that every domain report's finding statuses match the findings array.

- Severity: P3
- Confidence: High
- Area: ORCH
- Evidence:
  - `tools/full_domain.py:185-191` — `default_run()` prefixes the repo name although its own comment says ids must start `YYYYMMDD-HHMM-`
  - `automation/validation/audit_run_lifecycle.sh:120-122` — a run id must match `^[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{4}-`
  - current run id `falcon-20261011-0416-full-f5cb7c9` -> regex FAIL (tested); `20261011-0416-full-main-f5cb7c9` -> PASS
  - falcon PR #45 renamed already-published runs for exactly this reason
  - `docs/runbooks/AUDIT_RUN_LIFECYCLE.md:24-33` — run folders must pass the structural check
- What is happening: the run id produced for this run again starts with the repo name, so publishing it unchanged into `docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/` fails the target repo's lifecycle check and requires a rename commit.
- Why it matters: mechanical rework and a broken run record if published as-is.
- User / business impact: minor process friction.
- Security / privacy / reliability impact: none directly.
- Recommended fix: make `default_run()` emit `<timestamp>-<mode>-<branch>-<sha7>` (repo recorded in `scope.name` only) or auto-rename at publish; add a publish-time regex assertion. Note `tools/publish_audit.py` already defaults to a conforming id.
- Suggested validation: `audit_run_lifecycle.sh check` passes on the published folder without a rename.
- Owner suggestion: audit-tooling owner.
- Effort estimate: S.
- Dependencies: none.
- Status: still-open.
- Endpoint / data path: run id -> published folder -> lifecycle check.
- Attack path: none identified.

### ORCH-P3-002 - Domain report and findings array disagree on a finding status inside the same 20261009 run artifact

- Severity: P3
- Confidence: High (the same JSON file contains both values; reproduced by parsing it)
- Area: ORCH
- Evidence:
  - `runs/falcon-20261009-2117-full-08e20d1/_domains/02_architecture_runtime_topology.json` — the embedded `report` says `ARCH-P2-001 - Declared container hardening lags the running containers (verified fixed)` and `Status: verified-fixed`; the file's `findings` array records the same finding as `"status": "open"`
  - `runs/falcon-20261009-2117-full-08e20d1/follow_up_register.md:34` and `runs/falcon-20261011-0400-verify-main-584e1a3/follow_up_register.md:34` — `ARCH-P2-001 ... open`
  - live evidence at `f5cb7c9` supports fixed: `falcon_container_drift{kind="security"} 0` (fresh run 04:18Z) and live `no-new-privileges` on all inspected central/probe containers
- What is happening: the run's report body and its machine-readable findings disagree; the registers carried the machine value forward, so an already-fixed finding remains open in the register while the report claims closure.
- Why it matters: the aggregator and the release register cannot be trusted to reflect the audit's own conclusions without a manual re-check; the same class of contradiction (report vs register) is how ORCH-P2-001 arose.
- User / business impact: wrong open-work counts; reviewer confusion.
- Security / privacy / reliability impact: none directly; audit-record integrity.
- Recommended fix: reconcile ARCH-P2-001 in the register (append a note per lifecycle rule 1) and add a `check_run.sh` cross-check that every domain report's finding statuses match the findings array.
- Suggested validation: `check_run.sh` fails a synthetic run with a report/JSON status mismatch.
- Owner suggestion: audit-tooling owner.
- Effort estimate: S.
- Dependencies: none.
- Status: open.
- Endpoint / data path: `_domains/*.json` -> aggregate -> `follow_up_register.md`.
- Attack path: none identified.
